title: Harden file I/O: atomic scoring output, explicit UTF-8 encoding
description: From an independent UBS pass over session-touched code (0 critical, triage in comments): (1) the scoring script writes its output JSON non-atomically -- a kill mid-write leaves a truncated file that job() accepts by mtime freshness until the next run; write to .tmp then os.replace. (2) open() calls lack explicit encoding= (6 sites across scheduler and scoring script) -- deterministic on Linux but free portability robustness. False positives documented in the bead close: json.loads-no-try is the parser's pinned contract; Any typings are deliberate; logging/naive-datetime samples are unrelated lines.
close_reason: Independent UBS pass (0 critical) triaged: two real, the rest documented false positives. REAL FIXES: (1) scoring script output is now atomic -- write to a .tmp sibling (invisible to job()'s newest-*.json glob) then os.replace, closing the truncated-file-accepted-by-freshness window; CLI test asserts zero *.tmp residue; (2) explicit encoding='utf-8' on all six open() sites (scheduler x4, scoring script input+output) -- locale-independent I/O. FALSE POSITIVES documented: json.loads/load without try is the parser's pinned contract (raises JSONDecodeError loud; run_job_safely contains and retries; fuzz test pins it), Any typings are deliberate ORM/parser boundaries, logging/datetime findings sampled unrelated lines. UBS re-scan: warnings went 5 -> 5 only because the json.load finding remains (contract); encoding and print findings cleared from info tier. 59 passed; ruff/mypy clean.

title: Ingest upsert keyed with IP_address violates the (datetime, hostname) unique key
description: Fellow-agent deep review. ingest_data builds upsert conditions from datetime + hostname + IP_address, but both tables' unique constraints are (datetime, hostname) only. If a host's inventory IP changes between the original ingest and a re-ingest of the same combined file (retry after a failed scoring step, manual re-run), the query misses and the INSERT violates uix_1/uix_2 — IntegrityError, whole batch lost. First-principles: the natural key is (datetime, hostname); IP_address is run metadata, not part of the key. Fix: query by datetime+hostname only and update IP_address on the existing row.
close_reason: ingest_data upsert conditions now use the natural key (datetime, hostname) only — matching both tables' unique constraints — with IP_address updated as run metadata on existing rows (raw via the setattr loop, overall via setattr for the plugin-less mypy Column view). Proven failing-before: re-ingesting the same combined file after an inventory IP change raised IntegrityError (UNIQUE constraint failed datetime,hostname) and lost the whole batch. Regression test: two ingests with different IPs -> one raw + one overall row, both carrying the updated IP.

title: Use timezone-aware datetimes for staleness and API cutoffs
description: scheduler.py:140/:196 and api_routes.py:56/:77 use naive datetime.now()/fromtimestamp; local-time DST transitions can distort cutoffs and mtime staleness math. Adopt consistent timezone-aware now (UTC or local with tz) across scheduler staleness, ingestion timestamps, and API period cutoffs; keep DB semantics compatible.
close_reason: should_run_job now uses absolute epoch arithmetic (time.time() - getmtime) instead of naive datetime subtraction, eliminating the DST-distortion failure mode; storage/API sides documented as a shared local-naive convention (scheduler job timestamp = mtime; API cutoffs match). Full tz-aware UTC storage was evaluated and rejected: SQLite DateTime columns drop tzinfo on round-trip, so it would require migrating every existing DB row for no practical benefit in a single-operator tool — recorded in code comments at both sites. 46 passed; ruff/mypy/bandit clean.

title: Migrate ORM models to SQLAlchemy 2.0 Mapped/mapped_column (fix mypy gate on SQLAlchemy 2.1+) and wire documented .env defaults
description:
## Context & Vision Alignment
Supports Vision Goals V5 (Configuration & Operational Hygiene) and V6 (All Five Verify Gates Green).

## Observed Defects (Proven Failing-Before)
1. **Verify gate `mypy` is broken under current `sqlalchemy>=2.0,<3` (`sqlalchemy==2.1.4`, `mypy==2.4.0`)**:
   Running `mypy web_app/app script_to_generate_overall_benchmark_scores_from_subscores.py` fails with 2 errors:
   - `web_app/app/routes/api_routes.py:62:81: error: Argument 1 to "filter" of "Query" has incompatible type "bool"; expected "ColumnElement[bool] | ..." [arg-type]`
   - `web_app/app/routes/api_routes.py:83:83: error: Argument 1 to "filter" of "Query" has incompatible type "bool"; expected "ColumnElement[bool] | ..." [arg-type]`
   Root cause: `web_app/app/database/data_models.py` migrated `Base` to SQLAlchemy 2.0's `DeclarativeBase` (`ccea28c`), but left model attributes as legacy SQLAlchemy 1.x `Column(...)` instead of SQLAlchemy 2.0 `Mapped[...] = mapped_column(...)`. In SQLAlchemy 2.1+, `Column` inherits `Named[_T]` (`sqlalchemy/sql/_annotated_cols.py`), whose class-level `__get__(None, owner) -> Never` intentionally blocks ORM class-attribute access on unmapped `Column` objects. Thus `RawBenchmarkSubscores.datetime` types as `Never`, and `Never >= cutoff_date` resolves to `cutoff_date.__le__(...) -> bool`.
2. **Missing documented `.env` defaults in `decouple.config` calls**:
   `README.md` L195-200 documents defaults for all four configuration variables (`sqlite:///cloud_benchmarker.sqlite`, `360`, `my_ansible_inventory_file.ini`, `1000`), but `init_db.py:34`, `scheduler.py:22-23`, and `chart.py:20` call `config(...)` with no `default=` argument. Omitting any variable from `.env` (or running without `.env`) crashes at import time with `decouple.UndefinedValueError`.
3. **`.gitignore` missing `old_logs/`**:
   `logger_config.py` creates `old_logs/` and rotates files to `old_logs/cloud_benchmarker.log.1`, which does not match `*.log` in `.gitignore`.

## Implementation Plan
1. `web_app/app/database/data_models.py`:
   - Import `datetime as dt` (avoiding class-scope attribute `datetime` shadowing the type `dt.datetime`) and `Mapped, mapped_column` from `sqlalchemy.orm`.
   - Convert `RawBenchmarkSubscores` and `OverallNormalizedScore` columns from `Column(...)` to `Mapped[...] = mapped_column(...)`, preserving exact SQLite column types, `nullable=True`, `index=True`, `primary_key=True`, `autoincrement=True`, and `UniqueConstraint('datetime', 'hostname', ...)`.
2. `web_app/app/utils/scheduler.py`:
   - With `OverallNormalizedScore.IP_address` properly typed via `Mapped`, replace the `setattr(overall_record, "IP_address", ip_address)` workaround with direct attribute assignment `overall_record.IP_address = ip_address`.
   - Provide `default="my_ansible_inventory_file.ini"` and `default=360` in `decouple_config(...)` calls.
3. `web_app/app/database/init_db.py` & `web_app/app/chart.py`:
   - Provide `default="sqlite:///cloud_benchmarker.sqlite"` in `init_db.py` and `default=1000` in `chart.py`.
4. `.gitignore`:
   - Add `old_logs/` so rotated logs never dirty `git status`.

## Success Criteria & Regression Tests
- [ ] `mypy web_app/app script_to_generate_overall_benchmark_scores_from_subscores.py` exits 0 with 0 errors under `sqlalchemy==2.1.4` and `mypy==2.4.0`.
- [ ] Regression test in `tests/test_infra.py` verifying that when the 4 env vars are unset in a clean environment without `.env`, the modules fall back to the exact defaults documented in `README.md`.
close_reason: Migrated RawBenchmarkSubscores and OverallNormalizedScore in data_models.py from legacy Column(...) to SQLAlchemy 2.0 Mapped[...] = mapped_column(...) (using import datetime as dt to avoid class-scope name shadowing), fixing the 2 mypy arg-type errors on api_routes.py:62/:83 under SQLAlchemy 2.1.4 (where Column inherits Named[_T] and returns Never on class attribute access). Added the README-documented default values to all four decouple.config() calls (init_db.py, scheduler.py, chart.py) and added old_logs/ to .gitignore. Proven failing-before: mypy failed with 2 arg-type errors and importing without env/.env raised decouple.UndefinedValueError. Regression test test_documented_config_defaults_work_without_env_or_dotenv passes; mypy/ruff/bandit clean.

title: Verify cross-host score ranking live with different per-host values
description: The core value proposition -- min-max normalization RANKING across hosts with different values -- has never run in the real pipeline: both live E2Es produced identical values (same machine), so scoring only exercised the neutral-50 tie case live. Close it honestly with documented ansible mechanics: run the playbook once per single-host inventory (natural run-to-run noise yields different values), keep both fetch dirs, then run the REAL playbook with a two-host inventory and --start-at-task 'Combine benchmark results' so only the combine+scoring plays execute against the captured dirs. Assert: combined JSON has both hosts with different values, scoring output ranks them with non-trivial scores summing the contract, job() lands both rows with their distinct scores, CSV pairs each host with its own score, charts show both traces.
close_reason: Cross-host ranking verified LIVE for the first time using only real mechanics: two genuine single-host playbook runs captured per-host fetch dirs (values differ naturally run-to-run: hostB won cpu 15298.57 vs 12497.9, mutex 28.62 vs 65.4, threads 1.41 vs 1.91; hostA won memory 59301.73 vs 54910.77; fileio near-tied), then the real playbook's combine+scoring plays executed against the captured dirs via --start-at-task on the exact task name (first attempt failed: the flag matches task names, not play names). Scoring output: hostB 66.6666666667, hostA 33.3333333333 -- mathematically exact (400/6 and 200/6 under the playbook's custom weights: hostB took cpu+fileio+mutex+threads normalizations, hostA took memory), correctly ranked, dust-free (8i0 fix). Real job() landed both hosts with distinct scores; CSV paired each host with its OWN score; charts rendered both traces. Scratch removed; 59 tests green at HEAD.

title: Round final scores to 10 decimals so documented contract values are exact
description: Found by the localhost E2E run (cloud_benchmarker-evc): the playbook's real scoring output shows a single host at 49.99999999999999, but the docstring/CHANGELOG contract says tie/neutral hosts receive exactly 50. The clamp added in cloud_benchmarker-vgn only removes out-of-range dust; in-range dust from normalized-weight summation (weights sum to 1 only up to rounding) survives. Fix: round each final score to 10 decimal places (plus the existing clamp) — removes ~1e-14 dust, preserves all meaningful precision, makes the documented exact values (100 best, 50 neutral) hold under every weighting mode. Tighten the CLI test back to exact equality and add a single-host custom-weight neutral-50 assertion.
close_reason: calculate_overall_performance now clamps AND rounds each final score to 10 decimals. Defect found by the localhost E2E run: real playbook output showed a neutral-tie host at 49.99999999999999 instead of the documented 50 (normalized weights sum to 1 only up to float rounding; the vgn clamp only removed range exceedance). Regenerated the real playbook scoring output with system python3: exactly 50.0. Tests tightened to exact equality: single-host neutral 50.0, identical-hosts neutral 50.0, new single-host custom-weights regression test, CLI best-host == 100.0 exact. 53 passed; ruff/mypy clean.

title: Harden scoring engine against non-dict hosts, null/non-finite metrics, and empty host dicts; register module in pytest-cov
description:
## Context & Vision Alignment
Supports Vision Goals V2 (Direction-Aware Min-Max Scoring Engine) and V6 (100% Statement Coverage across both web_app and scoring script).

## Observed Defects (Proven Failing-Before)
1. **Per-host fault isolation missing in `script_to_generate_overall_benchmark_scores_from_subscores.py`**:
   While `scheduler.ingest_data` (`cloud_benchmarker-m8o`) and `data_models.py` (`cloud_benchmarker-ekf`) were hardened to tolerate malformed host entries and `None` metrics, `calculate_overall_performance` in the scoring script was not:
   - A non-dict host entry (e.g. `{"hostA": {...}, "hostList": ["not", "a", "dict"]}`) crashes with `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'keys'` (if first host) or treats list elements as metric names and raises `ValueError: Custom weights missing entries for metrics: ['not', 'a', 'dict']` (if later host).
   - A `None` (`null`) or non-numeric (`"bad"`, `True`) metric value crashes with `TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'float' and 'NoneType'` (or `'str'`), or treats `bool` as `1`/`0`.
   - A single `NaN` or `±Inf` metric value (accepted by `json.loads`) makes `max(reported)` / `min(reported)` evaluate to `nan`, poisoning `((val - min_value) / (max_value - min_value))` to `nan` for EVERY host, which `min(100.0, max(0.0, nan))` silently clamps to `0.0` for all hosts!
   - When hosts exist in `data` as valid dicts but all metric dicts are empty (e.g. `{"hostA": {}, "hostB": {}}` when all 5 sysbench tests failed), `calculate_overall_performance` returns `{}` (dropping all hosts) instead of assigning each valid host `NEUTRAL_SCORE = 50.0`.
2. **Coverage blind spot (`module-not-imported` warning)**:
   `tests/test_scoring.py` loads `script_to_generate_overall_benchmark_scores_from_subscores.py` via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("cb_scoring", ...)` without registering `script_to_generate_overall_benchmark_scores_from_subscores` in `sys.modules`. Running `pytest --cov=web_app --cov=script_to_generate_overall_benchmark_scores_from_subscores` emits `CoverageWarning: Module script_to_generate_overall_benchmark_scores_from_subscores was never imported`.

## Implementation Plan
1. `script_to_generate_overall_benchmark_scores_from_subscores.py`:
   - Define `_is_valid_metric_value(val: Any) -> bool`: `not isinstance(val, bool) and isinstance(val, (int, float)) and math.isfinite(val)`.
   - Filter `data` to `valid_hosts = {h: m for h, m in data.items() if isinstance(m, Mapping)}`. If `not valid_hosts`, return `{}`.
   - Collect `metrics` in encounter order across `valid_hosts` using only metrics where at least one host has `_is_valid_metric_value(val)`. (Keep existing `custom_weights` validation: if any metric in `metrics` is missing from `custom_weights`, raise `ValueError` as pinned by `test_custom_weights_are_normalized_and_missing_weight_rejected`.)
   - If `not metrics` (all valid hosts had empty dicts `{}` or only `None`/invalid values), return `{host: NEUTRAL_SCORE for host in valid_hosts}`.
   - For each `metric` in `metrics`, compute `reported = [float(valid_hosts[h][metric]) for h in host_names if metric in valid_hosts[h] and _is_valid_metric_value(valid_hosts[h][metric])]`. Any host without a valid finite number for `metric` receives `NEUTRAL_SCORE = 50.0` for that metric.
2. `tests/test_scoring.py`:
   - Register `sys.modules["script_to_generate_overall_benchmark_scores_from_subscores"] = scoring` before `_SPEC.loader.exec_module(scoring)` so `pytest-cov` tracks all statements in the scoring script with 100% coverage and zero warnings.
   - Add regression tests for `None` (`null`), `NaN`/`±Inf`, `bool`/string metric values, non-dict host entries, and all-empty host dicts `{}`.

## Success Criteria & Regression Tests
- [ ] `pytest --cov=web_app --cov=script_to_generate_overall_benchmark_scores_from_subscores` achieves 100% statement coverage on BOTH targets with zero `CoverageWarning`.
- [ ] All new regression tests fail on the old scorer and pass on the fixed scorer.
close_reason: Hardened script_to_generate_overall_benchmark_scores_from_subscores.py with _is_valid_metric_value (rejecting None, bool, non-numeric, and NaN/Inf), valid_hosts Mapping filter, neutral 50.0 fallback for empty host metric dicts, and extracted main(). Registered canonical module name in sys.modules in tests/test_scoring.py and added regression + in-process coverage tests; 93/93 statements (100% coverage) verified.

title: Raw data API 500s on partially-failed host runs (NULL metrics)
description: Fellow-agent deep review. The playbook omits metrics from failed sysbench tests by design (per-host dicts may lack keys; the scoring script documents 'hosts may report different metric subsets'), so RawBenchmarkSubscores rows legitimately carry NULL metric columns. But HistoricalRawBenchmarkSubscoresResponse declares all five metrics as non-Optional float — FastAPI response validation raises on the first partial row and /data/raw/ returns 500 for the entire endpoint, permanently for historical rows. First-principles: the response contract must mirror the storage contract (nullable metrics), not an idealized all-metrics row. Fix: Optional[float] = None on the five metric fields; verify charts/CSV already degrade gracefully (plotly gap, empty CSV cell).
close_reason: HistoricalRawBenchmarkSubscoresResponse metric fields are now Optional[float] = None, mirroring the storage contract. Discovered by fresh-eyes review of fellow agents' response-model contract vs the playbook's documented partial-subset behavior.

title: Normalize custom weights over active reported metrics, exclude zero-metric hosts from scoring/ingest, and harden missing-inventory/corrupt-combined-file handling
description:
## Summary & Background

During multi-mode reasoning (`M-DED` deductive invariant checking + `M-ADV` adversarial failure-mode analysis + Brenner falsifier triage) across the scoring engine, scheduler ingestion pipeline, and Ansible playbook, we identified two subtle mathematical and operational failure modes that occur when a benchmark run experiences partial or total test failures:

1. **Custom-Weight Normalization Under-Sum on Partial Metric Runs (`script_to_generate_overall_benchmark_scores_from_subscores.py`)**:
   - In `calculate_overall_performance(data, weighting="custom", custom_weights=...)`, `total_weight = sum(custom_weights.values())` sums over all keys in `custom_weights` (e.g., all 5 canonical metrics = `2.0 + 1.0 + 2.0 + 0.5 + 0.5 = 6.0`), whereas the score calculation `sum(n * weights[m] for n, m in zip(normalized_list, metrics))` only sums over the metrics actually reported in `data` (`metrics`).
   - When one or more sysbench tests fail across all hosts in a run (for example, `fileio` fails due to disk space, so `metrics` has 4 metrics instead of 5), the active weights sum to `5.0 / 6.0 = 0.8333333333` instead of `1.0`!
   - **Consequence**: A single host (or tied hosts) with 4 working metrics scores `41.6666666667` instead of the documented neutral `50.0`, and a host that is strictly best on all 4 reported metrics scores `83.3333333333` instead of `100.0`!
   - Furthermore, if one host in a multi-host run fails all 5 sysbench tests (`"hostDead": {}`), keeping `"hostDead": {}` in `valid_hosts` gives `hostDead` a neutral `50.0` on every metric, causing a 100%-failed host (`50.0`) to outrank a working slower host (`0.0`).
   - Additionally, negative or non-finite values in `custom_weights` were not rejected.

2. **All-Null Host Ingestion, Missing Inventory Resilience, and Playbook Fetch Guard (`web_app/app/utils/scheduler.py`, `benchmark-playbook.yml`)**:
   - In `ingest_data`: a host entry in `raw_data` with `{}` or all-`None` metric values (0 valid measurements) currently inserts an all-NULL `RawBenchmarkSubscores` row into SQLite. `ingest_data` should skip hosts that report zero non-`None` metric values.
   - In `parse_inventory`: if the inventory file is missing or unreadable (`OSError`) when `job()` runs, `parse_inventory` raises `FileNotFoundError` and aborts `job()`, losing the run's valid benchmark results even though `ingest_data` explicitly supports missing inventory mappings via `host_to_ip.get(hostname, 'UNKNOWN')`.
   - In `job()`: if `COMBINED_BENCHMARK_SUBSCORE_RESULTS_FILE_PATH` is missing or contains corrupt JSON (`(OSError, json.JSONDecodeError)`), `job()` should log a warning and return cleanly.
   - In `benchmark-playbook.yml`: only fetch per-host results when `benchmark_results | length > 0`, and clean `/tmp/{{ item }}_cloud_benchmarker_results` before fetching in Play 1 as well as after combining in Play 2.

## Implementation Plan

1. **`script_to_generate_overall_benchmark_scores_from_subscores.py`**:
   - Filter `valid_hosts` to mappings that contain at least one valid finite metric value (`any(_is_valid_metric_value(v) for v in scores.values())`).
   - In `weighting == "custom"`:
     - Validate that every weight in `custom_weights` for active `metrics` (and all values in `custom_weights`) is a finite non-negative number (`_is_valid_metric_value(w) and w >= 0`).
     - Normalize `weights` over the active `metrics` (`total_weight = sum(float(custom_weights[m]) for m in metrics)`), raising `ValueError` if `total_weight <= 0`.
2. **`web_app/app/utils/scheduler.py`**:
   - In `ingest_data`: if `not any(v is not None for v in sanitized_scores.values())`, log an error and skip the host so all-NULL rows are never inserted.
   - In `parse_inventory`: wrap `open(file_path, ...)` in `try ... except OSError:` that logs a warning and returns `{}` so ingestion proceeds with `IP_address='UNKNOWN'`.
   - In `job()`: guard `os.path.getmtime(COMBINED_BENCHMARK_SUBSCORE_RESULTS_FILE_PATH)` and `load_combined_results(...)` against `(OSError, json.JSONDecodeError)`, logging a warning and returning cleanly.
3. **`benchmark-playbook.yml`**:
   - Add `when: benchmark_results | length > 0` to `Fetch benchmark results to control node`.
   - Remove stale `/tmp/{{ inventory_hostname }}_cloud_benchmarker_results` on `localhost` (`delegate_to: localhost`, `become: false`) before fetching in Play 1 as well as after combining in Play 2.

## Verification & Acceptance Criteria

- Failing-before regression tests in `tests/test_scoring.py`:

title: Close scheduler ingest isolation bypasses (metadata column keys, non-numeric/bool/NaN raw metrics, partial re-ingest, corrupt overall JSON, tab/quoted inventory)
description:
## Context & Vision Alignment
Supports Vision Goal V3 (Resilient Scheduler & Isolated Per-Host Ingest).

## Observed Defects (Proven Failing-Before)
1. **Metadata column key injection bypasses `ingest_data` host isolation**:
   `scheduler.py:98` sets `raw_columns = set(RawBenchmarkSubscores.__table__.columns.keys())`, which includes `"id"`, `"datetime"`, `"hostname"`, and `"IP_address"`. A malformed host payload containing `"hostname"`, `"datetime"`, or `"IP_address"` passes `set(scores) - raw_columns` and raises `TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument ...` on `RawBenchmarkSubscores(**conditions, IP_address=ip_address, **scores)`, aborting `ingest_data` and losing the entire batch for all hosts! A payload containing `"id"` overwrites the primary key.
2. **Unvalidated raw metric value types & non-finite floats (`NaN`, `±Inf`)**:
   `scheduler.py` validates `overall_data[hostname]` is a non-bool number, but never validates values in `scores`:
   - String/collection values (e.g. `"not-a-float"`) raise `sqlalchemy.exc.StatementError` at flush/commit and roll back every good host in the batch.
   - Boolean values (`True`/`False`) silently persist as `1.0`/`0.0`.
   - Non-finite floats (`NaN`, `inf`, `-inf`) in either `scores` or `overall_data` persist into SQLite and then permanently 500 `/data/raw/` and `/data/overall/` (`ValueError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant`).
3. **Partial re-ingest leaves stale metric values on existing `RawBenchmarkSubscores` rows**:
   In `scheduler.py:126-128`, `for k, v in {**scores, "IP_address": ip_address}.items(): setattr(raw_record, k, v)` only updates keys present in `scores`. If a re-ingest of the same `(datetime, hostname)` omits a metric that was present earlier, the old value remains instead of resetting to `None`.
4. **Corrupt or non-dict `latest_overall_file` crashes `job()`**:
   In `scheduler.py:204-205`, `overall_data = json.load(f)` is unguarded against `(OSError, json.JSONDecodeError)` and does not check `isinstance(overall_data, dict)` (unlike `load_combined_results`). A corrupt or list/primitive overall file aborts the whole `job()` tick instead of degrading to raw-only ingestion.
5. **`parse_inventory` whitespace and quote sensitivity**:
   `scheduler.py:61-63` uses `stripped.split(' ', 1)[0]` (which fails when hostname and `ansible_host=` are separated by a tab `\t`) and does not strip quotes around `ansible_host="1.2.3.4"`.

## Implementation Plan
1. `web_app/app/utils/scheduler.py`:
   - Import `math` and `METRIC_COLUMNS` from `web_app.app.database.data_models`.
   - Define `_is_valid_number(value: Any) -> bool`: `not isinstance(value, bool) and isinstance(value, (int, float)) and math.isfinite(value)`.
   - In `ingest_data`:
     - Validate `unknown_keys = set(scores) - set(METRIC_COLUMNS)`.
     - Validate that every value `v` in `scores.values()` is either `None` or `_is_valid_number(v)`. If invalid, log an error naming the host and bad metric keys and `continue` (skipping that host before any DB mutation).
     - On update of an existing `raw_record`, set `raw_record.IP_address = ip_address` and for every `col` in `METRIC_COLUMNS`, `setattr(raw_record, col, scores.get(col))` so omitted metrics reset to `None`.
     - For `overall_data[hostname]`, validate `_is_valid_number(overall_data[hostname])`.
   - In `job()`:
     - Wrap reading `latest_overall_file` in `try ... except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError)` and verify `isinstance(loaded_overall, dict)`; on failure or non-dict, log a warning and keep `overall_data = {}` so raw subscores still ingest.
   - In `parse_inventory`:
     - Extract hostname with `stripped.split()[0]` and strip surrounding `'"` quotes from `match.group(1)`.

## Success Criteria & Regression Tests
- [ ] Regression tests in `tests/test_scheduler.py` covering metadata-key injection (`"hostname"`, `"id"`), string/bool/`NaN`/`±Inf` raw and overall values (and verifying `/data/raw/` and `/data/overall/` remain 200), partial re-ingest metric clearing to `None`, corrupt/non-dict overall JSON file fallback in `job()`, and tab/quoted inventory lines.
close_reason: Hardened scheduler.py: validated raw subscore keys against set(METRIC_COLUMNS) (blocking metadata column keyword collisions), validated raw and overall values with _is_valid_number (rejecting non-numeric strings, booleans, and NaN/Inf while preserving None for omitted raw metrics), cleared omitted METRIC_COLUMNS to None on re-ingest, guarded latest_overall_file json.load against OSError/JSONDecodeError and non-dict JSON, and hardened parse_inventory for tab-separated and quoted ansible_host values. Added 4 regression tests in tests/test_scheduler.py; 184/184 statements (100% coverage) verified.

title: Bound historical CSV merge_asof with temporal tolerance, sort chart traces chronologically, and harden benchmark-playbook.yml
description:
## Context & Vision Alignment
Supports Vision Goals V1 (Ansible Playbook Orchestration) and V4 (FastAPI Data, Charts & Historical CSV Endpoints).

## Observed Defects (Proven Failing-Before)
1. **Cross-run stale score misattribution in `/benchmark_historical_csv/` (`web_app/app/routes/api_routes.py:140-146`)**:
   `get_benchmark_historical_csv` calls `pd.merge_asof(..., on="datetime", by="hostname", direction="nearest")` with NO `tolerance`. When `hostA` has an `OverallNormalizedScore` row on Run 1 (e.g. 5 days ago, `85.0`) and Run 2 (today) ingested only `RawBenchmarkSubscores` (because scoring failed or was rejected as stale by `scheduler.py`), `merge_asof` silently attaches Run 1's 5-day-old `85.0` score onto Run 2's CSV row!
2. **Reverse-chronological chart DataFrames (`web_app/app/chart.py:102-122`)**:
   `generate_benchmark_charts` queries `ORDER BY datetime DESC LIMIT MAX_DATA_POINTS_FOR_CHART` to bound the query to the most recent N rows, but never sorts `raw_df` or `overall_df` ascending by `datetime` before constructing the Plotly figures. Line and spline traces are emitted backwards in time (newest-to-oldest), contradicting `README.md` L172 and L188.
3. **Playbook edge-case hazards (`benchmark-playbook.yml`)**:
   - Play 2 (`Combine benchmark results`) iterates over `groups['all']` and reads `/tmp/${host}_cloud_benchmarker_results/cloud_benchmarker_results.json`. Because those `/tmp` directories are never removed after Play 2/3, if a host succeeded yesterday and is unreachable today, Play 2 silently combines yesterday's leftover `/tmp` file into today's benchmark results.
   - Play 1's FileIO shell task runs `set -e` then `sysbench fileio prepare`, `sysbench fileio ... run`, `sysbench fileio cleanup`. If `run` fails, `set -e` exits before `cleanup`, leaking 128 test files (2 GiB) on the target host.
   - Play 1's 5 sysbench shell tasks extract metrics via `grep ... | awk ...` without asserting the extracted string is non-empty (`[ -n "$..." ]`). If `grep` finds no match, `awk` still exits 0 with an empty string, echoing invalid JSON `{"metric": }` with `rc=0`, which then crashes `set_fact` (`from_json`) without `ignore_errors` and aborts the entire host play.

## Implementation Plan
1. `web_app/app/routes/api_routes.py`:
   - Pass `tolerance=pd.Timedelta(seconds=30)` to `pd.merge_asof` in `get_benchmark_historical_csv`. Since the scheduler's minimum run interval is clamped to 1 minute (60s) and same-run raw/overall timestamps match (or are within seconds in synthetic fixtures), a 30-second tolerance pairs same-run scores while leaving `overall_score` empty (`""`) for runs whose overall score is missing.
2. `web_app/app/chart.py`:
   - After converting `raw_df['datetime']` and `overall_df['datetime']` with `pd.to_datetime`, sort both DataFrames ascending by `datetime` (`sort_values('datetime', kind='mergesort').reset_index(drop=True)`).
3. `benchmark-playbook.yml`:
   - In the FileIO shell task, add `trap 'sysbench fileio cleanup >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT` immediately before `sysbench fileio prepare` so cleanup always runs even if `prepare` or `run` fails.
   - In all 5 sysbench shell tasks, add `test -n "$..."` on the extracted metric value before `echo "{...}"` so an empty extraction exits nonzero and is cleanly skipped by `ignore_errors: yes` + `when: ... is not failed`.
   - At the end of Play 3 (`Copy and execute Python script`), clean up the consumed `/tmp/{{ item }}_cloud_benchmarker_results` directories (preserving `--start-at-task` compatibility for Play 2 while preventing stale `/tmp` files from surviving into future runs).

## Success Criteria & Regression Tests
- [ ] Regression test in `tests/test_api.py` proving that when a host has a full run at `t1` and a raw-only run at `t2` (hours/days later), `/benchmark_historical_csv/` pairs `t1` with its score and leaves `t2`'s `overall_score` empty (`""`).
- [ ] Regression test in `tests/test_api.py` / `tests/test_chart.py` proving that `generate_benchmark_charts` orders multi-timestamp traces chronologically (oldest to newest).
- [ ] `ansible-playbook --syntax-check -i my_ansible_inventory_file.ini benchmark-playbook.yml` passes clean.
close_reason: Added tolerance=pd.Timedelta(seconds=30) to pd.merge_asof in web_app/app/routes/api_routes.py to prevent stale cross-run overall_score pairing; sorted raw_df and overall_df ascending by datetime in web_app/app/chart.py; hardened benchmark-playbook.yml with non-empty metric guards, trap-based fileio cleanup, and per-host /tmp directory cleanup; added regression tests in tests/test_api.py and tests/test_chart.py. Verified 70/70 tests passing with 511/511 statements (100% coverage) and ansible-playbook --syntax-check green.

title: Compare overall-file freshness with mtime, not ctime, in job()
description: job() picks the latest overall-scores file by os.path.getctime and checks getctime(latest_overall_file) >= datetime_from_file.timestamp() (scheduler.py ~187) — but datetime_from_file derives from the combined file's mtime. On Linux ctime is inode-change time, not creation: any metadata touch (chmod/chown/cp) bumps ctime above mtime, so a STALE overall file from a previous run can pass the freshness check and get mislabeled as this run's scores. Normalize both sides to mtime; regression-test with a file whose ctime > mtime (os.utime old mtime then chmod).
close_reason: job() now compares overall-file freshness with os.path.getmtime on BOTH sides (previously: ctime for the overall file vs an mtime-derived timestamp for the combined file). On Linux ctime is inode-change time, so chmod/chown/backup touches made a stale file look fresh and mislabel a previous run's scores onto current rows. Regression test deterministically reproduces the old failure: os.utime sets mtime 2h back, chmod bumps ctime to now — old code ingests the stale scores, new code rejects them. Existing stale-rejection test still green. 50 passed; ruff/mypy/bandit clean.
